The most informative thing is to look at stack sizes, which you can tell by the all-in amount, relative to the blinds. In this case the blinds are 10k/20k with a 3k ante. That means each rotation around the table the player is losing 10k + 20k + 3k * playersRemaining. If it was heads up, that's 36k. Now divide the stack sizes by this 36k and you get 880k / 36k = 24 for the short stack. That number tells you how aggressively you need to play. It depends on the tournament format, but in the early stages of a tournament players might start with a value in the hundreds. 24 an upper low value meaning very aggressive play is in order. Keep in minds the blinds, or prices you pay per round, constantly increase as well.

This is actually a mathematical problem. An unexploitable range can be used by calculating out the nash equilibrium ranges. Here they are for heads up with limited stack sizes. So table would stop applying once we start getting into the 30+ range for that number we calculated above. Most amateur players are far too conservative and spend more time trying to soul read, and folding, than focusing on the math. It's silly and exploitable which is why it's possible to win at poker. But suffice to say that 99 is way above the range both players should be willing to get it all in with and happily call of their stacks with. So neither play can be said to have made a mistake in this hand almost regardless of how it played out.

Luck all depends on how you look at things. These players probably got it in on an early street, and I'd assume preflop - before the first three 'public' cards are shown. And in that case the 99 will still win about 20% of the time. Sucks to lose on the final card, but in the end it'll happen tens of thousands of times if you play long enough - and it has no effect on whether you come out a winner or a loser in the longrun. And this is before we get into a discussion about playing versus ranges and not versus hands when luck becomes even more pointless a concept. It's still there of course, just not in the way you think it is.
